title: CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval
description: Hardcoded CSP disables XSS mitigation app-wide
recommendation: Remove unsafe directives; introduce per-request CSP nonce middleware; coordinate with frontend Vite build

title: No CSP meta tag and Vite build uses eval-adjacent features
description: `index.html` has no Content-Security-Policy meta tag. Vite's React plugin in dev uses `eval` for HMR. Production build uses Terser (safe) but no CSP is set at the HTML layer. Scope 08 audit F-08-003 found backend CSP hardcodes `unsafe-inline unsafe-eval` — the frontend does not add a compensating stricter CSP at the HTML level either. Any XSS in the app has no CSP mitigation.
recommendation: Add `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` to `index.html` with `script-src 'self'`; use nonces for any inline scripts. Remove `unsafe-eval` from nginx/backend CSP (scope 08 F-08-003 fix). Configure Vite to emit nonce-based CSP header.
acceptance_test_hint: Lighthouse security audit shows CSP present; browser DevTools shows no CSP violation on page load

title: CSP allows `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` for scripts
description: `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' ...`. Defeats CSP's main purpose against XSS. The frontend variant (security-headers.conf in frontend/) does NOT include these — divergence.
recommendation: Remove `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` from script-src; use nonces or hashes for any required inline.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -sI https://host/ | grep -i content-security | grep -v "'unsafe-eval'"` returns the header
